latin_text: above the heavens, the waters are the minds of the cherubim. But see what a disparity of condition there is in the same nature: the elemental moisture quenches the heat of life; the celestial feeds it; the supercelestial understands it.
english_translation: above the heavens, the waters are the minds of the cherubim. But see what a disparity of condition there is in the same nature: the elemental moisture quenches the heat of life; the celestial feeds it; the supercelestial understands it.
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico identifies Cherubim with the minds (*mentes*) that constitute intelligible forms—the second-highest angelic order embodies cosmic understanding. The passage emphasizes the paradox of identity-in-difference: water exists at three levels with opposite functions. Elementally, moisture quenches heat (opposes life); celestially, water feeds heat (sustains life); superceles­tially, water is pure intellection understanding both. [INFERRED] This demonstrates how identical substances possess contradictory properties at different ontological levels—the principle that justifies both correspondence magic and mystical transformation.

The philosophical function is to ground Cherubim as the principle of *mediation and understanding*. Cherubim do not merely contemplate forms but *are* forms, and their intellection is the very structure through which all lower orders participate in intelligible reality. [INFERRED] This is why the Oration (O.1.8) associates Cherubim with contemplative wisdom and intellectual light.

[VERIFIED] Commento (C.3.3) develops the Cherubim-Binah correspondence. Being & Unity grounds it: Cherubim exemplify participated understanding at the highest creaturely level.
notes: HARVESTER passage: H.SP.4 | Cherubim as intelligence and intelligible forms; cherubic knowledge as cosmic understanding
